answer: Before an agent may sell a load of timber, the state forestry office checks its harvest permit number against the tract map and the scale ticket written at a certified mill. A permit tag that appears on two loads trips a timber trespass action, suspends the permit and calls the logger surety bond. A permit costs 240, certified scaling 65 per load and the bond 1400, so N fakes cost N x 1705 and each still needs a felled tract and a truck. A river drive of cheap identities, a hollow claim about ownership and an atlas of copied tract maps change none of that.
